title.name: Cose Preziose
title.warn: Contains jump scares, flickering lights and gruesome scenes. Play in landscape, ideally with headphones. Scares and flashing can be reduced in the settings.
intro.1:
October 1974.
The last letter from my sister Lisa arrived three weeks late.
intro.2: "Diego, a stranger has come to {{name.village}}. He opened a shop beneath Dad's butcher's. He sells beautiful things, almost for free. Dad isn't himself anymore. Please come home."
intro.3:
I came home.
There was no one at the station. Not even the stationmaster.
intro.4:
In the village they told me Lisa is dead.
No one would tell me how.
ui.useHint: tap where to use it, or tap again to examine
ui.diaryEmpty: No pages yet. Lisa left them around the village.
map.intro1: {{name.village}}. It looks like everyone has left.
map.intro2: Below Dad's shop there's a light on. A new sign: Emporio.
map.notYet: The butcher's shutter is half down. First I want to see who opened that shop underneath: the Emporium, the dark door on the right.
map.butcherClosed: I'm not going back in. Not now. He's still in there.
map.barberLocked: The barber's. The curtains are drawn.
map.barberDone: There's nothing I need in there anymore.
map.soon: Closed. This part of the village comes in the next version.
map.alley: The alley is full of fog. Someone is crying down there. Not yet.
map.station: No trains leaving. The next one, says the sign, "when it's over".
end.1:
Five objects are back in their place.
One is missing.
end.2:
Somewhere in the shops, Lisa has left messages.
St Michael's is waiting.
end.3:
Thank you for playing.
Tell us what scared you.
item.photo.desc: A photograph of the barber's shop.
item.case.desc: A case with a letter padlock.
item.razor.desc: It's warm. As if someone had just been holding it.
hint.notYet: There's no one to call yet.
hint.none: You call Lisa, but she doesn't answer. She has spent too much of herself on you here.
hint.generic: Look carefully, Diego. Things here always have two faces.
hint.map.emporio: He's waiting for you. Under the butcher's.
hint.map.macelleria: Our home. The butcher's. I need to talk to you.
hint.map.barbiere: The barber, Diego. The shop with the striped pole.
hint.map.return: Take the razor to the Emporium. Before he wants it back.
hint.emporio.go: Don't trust him. But for now, do what he says.
hint.emporio.place: The display case. There's an empty place with their name on it.
hint.emporio.done: Five are safe. That's enough for now.
hint.bar.fuse: The fuse box needs a fuse. Barbers keep everything in drawers, under the mirror.
hint.bar.useFuse: Tap the fuse in the apron, then the fuse box on the left wall.
hint.bar.steam: The towel steamer makes steam. Steam fogs mirrors. And people write on fogged mirrors.
hint.bar.till: The bill written on the mirror, and the price list on the wall. Add it up: that's the number for the till.
hint.bar.chairs: Look at the photo: that day the chairs were turned differently. Each tap turns one a quarter.
hint.bar.cabinet: The little key is as small as the lock on the back-room door, on the left wall.
hint.bar.case: The letters on the case are written backwards. Read them from the right, or show them to the shop mirror.
hint.bar.leave: Get out of here, Diego. He's watching you from the mirror.
diary.lisa1.title: Day 23
diary.lisa1.text:
Dad laughed today. I hadn't heard him laugh since Mum died. He was laughing alone, in the cold room, with that thing in his hand.
The stranger says it's a gift. He says a small favour is all he asks in return.
I saw the favour. It was a delivery. It was wrapped in the apron.
If you read this, Diego, don't look him in the eye.
diary.lisa2.title: Day 27
diary.lisa2.text:
Today Mr Aldo trimmed my hair. His hands were smooth like a boy's, and he told me that since he got his new razor he doesn't feel old anymore.
Then he looked in the mirror and stopped talking. As if he expected to see someone else.
He held the razor tight the whole time. He wouldn't let me touch it.
note.merchant: The Merchant wants me to bring back the things he sold. He says they "have served their time".
note.ledger: Dad's ledger: every Tuesday a delivery "downstairs". Last line: "The favour is paid".
note.barber: Lisa: the barber bought something from the Emporium too.
note.mirror: On the barber's mirror: "The stranger's bill: two shaves and one tonic".
note.prices: Price list: haircut 600, shave 350, shampoo 250, tonic 150, child's cut 400 lire.
note.receipt: Receipt in the till: "Received: one razor. Price: a small favour. — The Merchant".
note.caseWord: In the mirror, the letters on the case read the right way round.
emp.intro1: There you are. I've been expecting you. You have your sister's eyes.
emp.intro2: Who are you? What do you know about Lisa?
emp.intro3: Just a shopkeeper. I sell precious things to those who truly want them. The price is always fair.
emp.intro4: But some of my goods have served their time. They must come back here, where they can do no more harm. Someone has already started: look at the display case.
emp.intro5: And why should I do it?
emp.intro6: Because you came back. And as long as those objects stay out there, this village doesn't sleep. Not even its dead.
emp.intro7: Start at home, Diego. Your father's shop is right upstairs.
emp.again: Still here? Time passes for the dead too, Diego.
emp.afterButcher1: You've seen your father again, I see. He always had a temper.
emp.afterButcher3: I know many things. The barber, for instance, has a razor that no longer belongs to him. Bring it to me.
emp.feelRazor: I can feel it from here. You have something for me. Put it in the display case, in its place.
emp.haveRazor: Not to me. In the display case. Everything has its place.
emp.notToMe: I won't touch it. Put it in the case.
emp.sealed: The glass fogs over, then clears. For a moment every candle flame bends towards the case.
emp.placed1: One. Can you hear the village breathing easier?
emp.placed2: Five more, Diego. And the more you bring back, the darker the night.
emp.placed3: ...Why do I feel like you're the one who profits?
emp.after1: Come back when you have another.
emp.after2: And give my regards to your sister.
emp.slotEmpty: An empty pedestal. The tag says: {name}.
emp.slotFull: The razor is in its place. I never want to touch it again.
emp.case1: A shoe, a statuette, a doll. And two things wrapped in cloth, tagged with the butcher's and the Valigia dei Sogni.
emp.case2: Below, six empty pedestals. Six tags. The last one says: Lisa.
emp.shelves: Books, a globe, a brass angel, a doll with black eyes. Nothing has a price. I feel like something is following me with its eyes.
emp.ledger1: A ledger. Names from the village, one per line. Next to each: "favour paid".
emp.ledger2: One doesn't read other people's accounts, Diego. It's rude.
mac.enter2: The neon hums. The counter is full, as if the shop was open yesterday.
mac.enter3: A sound from the cold room. Drips. Then nothing.
mac.counter1: The meat is laid out with care. On the tags: "Tongue". "Fingers, per 100 g".
mac.counter2: Among the cuts there's a hand. I don't want to know whose.
mac.ledgerText:
Tuesday — 2 kg rib, Mrs Ada
Tuesday — delivery DOWNSTAIRS
Tuesday — delivery DOWNSTAIRS
Tuesday — delivery DOWNSTAIRS
...
14 October — The favour is paid.
mac.scale: The scale reads zero. But the pan is dirty.
mac.photo1: Our photo. Dad, Mum, Lisa and me, in front of the shop.
mac.photo2: Someone has scratched out Dad's face.
mac.cella: The cold room door is shut. On the other side, something leans against the metal.
mac.hooks: The hooks sway gently. There's no air in here.
mac.stairs: The door up to our home. It's blocked from the other side.
mac.lisa3: You shouldn't have come back. He called you, didn't he? The Merchant.
mac.lisa4: Dad is gone. There's only what the object left of him. And it isn't finished.
mac.lisa5: What did he do to you?
mac.lisa6: Not now. The barber, Diego. He bought something too. Don't look in the mirror for too long.
mac.lisa7: If you get lost, call me. But I can't do it often. It costs me.
mac.diaryGiven: A page of Lisa's diary slips out of the ledger and falls at your feet.
mac.caught: A huge hand brushes the back of your neck. You trip, you roll, the door, the street.
mac.outside1: It was Dad. It was his voice.
mac.outside2: The barber. Lisa said the barber.
bar.enter1: The shop is dark. All three chairs face the right-hand wall, as if someone turned them on purpose.
bar.enter2: The mirror takes up the whole wall. I don't like the way it looks at me.
bar.mirrorRead: Someone has written on the fogged mirror with a finger: "The stranger's bill: two shaves and one tonic".
bar.mirrorThink: The bill. I need the price list.
bar.mirrorLit: My reflection looks more tired than I am.
bar.mirrorDark: In the dark the mirror is a black slab. For a moment my reflection seemed to move a beat late.
bar.calendar: The calendar stopped in October. The 14th is circled three times.
bar.fuseMissing: The fuse box. A fuse is missing.
bar.drawer: Combs, rusty scissors... and a fuse, wrapped in a handkerchief.
bar.noPower: Nothing works in here without power. I need to get the lights back on first.
bar.steamDone: The towel steamer is still warm.
bar.tooDark: Even with the torch, the writing on the price list is too faded. I need to get the power back on in here first.
bar.tillOpen: DING! The till drawer opens. No money: a photograph, a receipt and a page folded in four.
bar.photoBack: On the back: "The day he arrived. I want to remember it like this, everything as it was."
bar.chairsOpen: Click. The footrest of the middle chair springs forward. Something was hidden underneath.
bar.cabinetLocked: The razor cabinet. Locked, a small keyhole.
bar.caseFound: The leather case. It's heavier than it should be.
bar.case1: A leather case with a four-letter padlock.
bar.case2: On the lid, letters engraved backwards, as if meant to be read in a mirror: E M I T.
bar.reflect: In the mirror the letters turn the right way round. I write them down before they change their mind.
bar.razor1: A razor with an ivory handle. The blade is red, as if it had just been used.
bar.razor2: Behind you, the mirror fogs up again. On its own.
bar.ghost1: In the reflection someone stands behind you. An old man. He's looking at your throat.
bar.after1: There's no one. There's no one.
bar.after2: I have to take it to the Emporium. Now.
mac.enterHint: If Dad left anything behind, it's here: the counter, his delivery ledger, our photo on the left wall.
emp.torch1: Ah, one last thing. Take this: a gift from the house. It's dark out there, and I wouldn't want you to trip just now.
emp.torch2: A heavy metal torch. When you switch it on, the light trembles for a moment.
bar.retroLocked: The back-room door. "Private". Locked, a small keyhole.
bar.retroOpen: The little key turns. The door opens by itself, slowly, into the dark: as if someone on the other side were pulling it.
bar.pulled: Your legs carry you up the stairs, into the shop, in front of the mirror. You didn't decide to go.
hint.bar.goRetro: The case isn't here. The barber hid things down below. Go through the back room.
retro.enter1: The back room smells of brilliantine and mould.
retro.enter2: A sink, a boiler, a dusty bench. And a trapdoor in the floor.
retro.cloth: A rough cloth, still damp. I'll keep it in my hand: it may be useful.
retro.sink: The little mirror over the sink is filthy. The tap gives no water: the boiler is off.
retro.sinkClock: On the fogged mirror someone has drawn a clock with a finger. Ten past ten.
retro.bench: The dust on the bench has left five clean circles of different sizes. The bottles are all crowded at the front. I can drag them with my finger.
retro.benchDone: Every bottle is back in its circle.
retro.tooBig: No: the bottle is wider than that ring.
retro.tooSmall: No: that ring is bigger than this bottle.
retro.drawerOpen: Clack. The bench drawer has opened by itself.
retro.crank: An iron crank with a worn wooden handle.
retro.plateDirty: There's a brass plate on the boiler, black with soot. You can't read a thing: I need something to clean it with.
retro.plateRub: The plate is black with soot. With the cloth I could clean it: rub over it with your finger.
retro.valvesHint: Three red handwheels. Turn them by moving your finger in a circle over them.
retro.boilerDone: The boiler gurgles. Something inside it is breathing.
retro.fogClock1: The hot water fogs the little mirror. On the steam a drawing appears, made with a finger: a clock. Ten past ten.
retro.trapLocked: A trapdoor in the floor. No handle, just a square hole beside it: a crank goes there.
retro.crankIn: The crank fits the hole. Now it has to be turned, clockwise.
retro.turnCrank: I have to turn the crank: put your finger on it and move it round in circles, three turns.
retro.trapOpen: The trapdoor opens. Cold air rises from below, and a cellar smell. And something like a breath.
retro.helmet: A hair-dryer hood. Inside, a lock of white hair.
hint.retro.cloth: Take the cloth by the sink. You'll need it for cleaning.
hint.retro.bottles: Go to the bench: drag each bottle into the clean ring of its size.
hint.retro.drawer: The bench drawer has opened. Take what's inside.
hint.retro.plate: With the cloth in hand, rub the black plate on the boiler.
hint.retro.valves: Turn the three red wheels to the numbers on the plate, left to right: 2, 7, 4.
hint.retro.crankIn: Use the crank on the hole next to the trapdoor.
hint.retro.crank: Turn the crank with your finger, clockwise, until the trapdoor opens.
hint.retro.down: Go down, Diego. But don't stop in front of the mirrors.
note.clock: Back-room mirror: a clock at ten past ten, and the word "young".
item.crank.desc: An iron crank. It's for turning something.
cantina.enter1: A cellar. It's cold, and it smells of wine gone bad.
cantina.enter2: Everywhere, things covered with sheets. As tall as people.
cantina.sheet: Something covered with a sheet. To take it off I have to pull it down with my finger.
cantina.mirror: A mirror. There are many down here. He covered them all.
cantina.glimpse: Someone was behind me. In the mirror. An old man in a white coat.
cantina.clockFound: Under the sheet there's a grandfather clock. Stopped at 3:33.
cantina.clock: The hands can be turned: finger in a circle on the long hand.
cantina.clockOpen: Tack. The pendulum door opens. Inside there's a leather case.
cantina.clockEmpty: The pendulum doesn't move. But I can hear it ticking anyway.
cantina.wall2: Take me back to when I opened the shop.
cantina.rack: Bottles of wine. The labels all say the same year: 1951.
cantina.oldChair: An old barber's chair, broken. The leather has been slashed. Many times.
hint.cantina.sheets: Pull the sheets down. One hides something that isn't a mirror.
hint.cantina.clock: The back-room mirror already told you the time. And the torch reads the writing on the walls.
hint.cantina.take: Take the case from the clock.
hint.cantina.up: Open the case. And then get out of this cellar.
mem.bar.title: Memory — Aldo, the barber
mem.bar.1: 1951. Aldo Morandi opens his shop on the square. He's twenty-three, with the steadiest hands in the village and a smile that keeps customers coming back.
mem.bar.2: The years go by in the same mirror. Every morning Aldo finds a slightly older man in it. He starts to hate him.
mem.bar.3: In October 1974 a stranger dressed in black gives him an ivory-handled razor. "Every shave will give you back a year." In return, a small favour.
mem.bar.4: The favour: keep working. Every customer gets up from the chair a year older. Aldo grows younger, the village grows old, and nobody understands why.
mem.bar.5: One morning Aldo looks in the mirror and can no longer see himself. He can only see out from inside it. Since then he has been waiting, behind the glass, for someone to bring the razor back.
diary.memBarbiere.title: Memory: Aldo, the barber
diary.memBarbiere.text:
1951: Aldo Morandi opens his shop, aged twenty-three.
The years go by in the same mirror, and Aldo starts to hate it.
October 1974: the stranger in black gives him an ivory razor. "Every shave will give you back a year."
The favour: keep working. Every customer gets up a year older, Aldo grows younger, the village grows old.
One morning Aldo can no longer see himself in the mirror. He can only see out from inside it.
map.adaLocked: Mrs Ada's house. Shutters closed. Not yet.
map.adaDone: Ada's house is quiet now. Even the rocking chair.
mid.1:
One object is back where it belongs.
Five to go.
mid.2:
As you cross the square, a shutter creaks.
The village has noticed you.
hint.map.ada: Mrs Ada's house, Diego. She never really left.
hint.map.returnGlasses: Bring the glasses to the Emporium. She wants them back.
hint.map.done: That's enough for now, Diego. Rest, if you can.
hint.emporio.ada: Go to Mrs Ada's. The house near the fountain.
ada.enter1: Mrs Ada's house. When we were kids she gave us mint sweets.
ada.enter2: It smells shut in. And of tea left to go cold for years.
ada.tvOn: The TV hums into life. Just snow. But the snow... seems to breathe.
ada.tvSnow: Snow. Somewhere underneath, someone is talking.
ada.tvAfter: Only snow now. He said what he had to say.
ada.tv2: I can't leave while you're looking.
ada.tv3: I locked them in the trunk. Our day... our day is the key.
ada.tv4: Her husband. Ettore. Speaking from the TV.
ada.guideTitle: TV guide — week of 9 to 15 June 1974
ada.guide3: Channel 5 — 9:00 pm — "The Parlour of Those Who Stay" — circled in pen, three times
ada.guide5: In the margin, in Ada's shaky hand: "Every evening he's there."
ada.photo1: Ada and Ettore, young, cheek to cheek. She barely smiles; he looks like he's just said something silly. There's writing on the back.
ada.photoBackTitle: On the back of the photo
ada.photoBack:
Our table: me by the stove, you by the window,
the teapot between us
and the sugar bowl always on your side, you sweet tooth.
You with your chipped cup, me with the wisteria one.
Forever.

A. — 14 June 1946
ada.rocker: Ettore's rocking chair. The cushion still holds the shape of his back. It rocks slowly, on its own, back and forth.
ada.rockerAfter: It's rocking harder now. As if Ettore had just got up in a hurry.
ada.wheelchair: Ada's wheelchair. Turned to face the wall, like a punishment.
ada.giveBack: They're mine... give them back. I want to see him again...
ada.sorry: I'm sorry, Mrs Ada. You have to let him go.
ada.hatchHigh: The attic hatch. The cord is too high, I can't reach it.
ada.hatchOpen: I hook the cord with the crutch. The hatch swings open and the ladder comes down on its own.
ada.rack: Ettore's fishing hat. Still hanging there, as if he were going out in the morning.
ada.kitchen1: The kitchen. On the table, a teapot, a sugar bowl and four odd cups.
ada.kitchen2: Every evening she laid the table for two. Even after.
ada.table: Four cups, a teapot, a sugar bowl. Only two cups were theirs, and each had their place: the window on one side, the stove on the other.
ada.tableAfter: The table is laid. The chair by the window has been pulled out.
ada.wrongSeat: No... that's not his place. They sat differently in the photo.
ada.pantryOpen: The pantry has opened by itself. Inside, hanging on a nail, there's a key.
ada.pantryShut: The pantry won't open. There's no lock. It's as if someone were holding it shut from inside.
ada.pantryEmpty: The pantry is empty. Only jars of jam with handwritten dates.
ada.crutch: One of Ettore's crutches. He came back from the war like that.
ada.kettleOn: I switch on the ring under the kettle. The coil turns grey, then white.
ada.kettleAfter: The kettle is still warm. The window stays fogged up.
ada.stove: An electric cooker. The knob is worn in one spot only: always the same ring.
ada.window: Outside, bare trees. A grey light comes through the glass.
ada.windowFog: The writing is still there on the fogged glass. From outside.
ada.fogSeen: Someone wrote it with a finger... on the outside of the glass.
ada.sink: Two cups washed and left to drain in the sink. Dust on them.
ada.calText:
June 1974. The 14th is circled: "28 years".
Nobody tore off the pages after the 17th.
At the bottom, in pencil, in her handwriting:
"Don't throw away E.'s chipped cup: it's the one from our first coffee.
Mine is the one with the wisteria, he gave it to me."
ada.attic1: The attic. Low, dusty. The bulb died long ago.
ada.attic2: At the back, a trunk. Crates stacked in front of it, as if to hide it.
ada.trunkBlocked: The crates are in front of the trunk. I have to move them.
ada.trunkOpen: The trunk opens. On the wedding veil, a pair of round glasses. They glow red.
ada.ghost3: They found her up here, kneeling in front of the trunk. Wearing the glasses.
ada.dummy: Ada's wedding dress, on a tailor's dummy. Yellowed. The sleeves stir, but there's no draught.
ada.letter:
"My Ada, when I come home I won't be the man I was. But I'll look at you as I did on the first day, and you'll do the same. Forever.
Yours, Ettore"
note.channel: TV guide: channel 5 is circled three times.
note.seats: Photo: he by the window, she by the stove, the teapot between them, the sugar bowl on his side. 14 June 1946.
note.trunk: Ettore: "Our day is the key" — the trunk in the attic.
hint.ada.tv: Switch on the TV, Diego. He still talks.
hint.ada.channel: The channel... look at the guide on the sofa: she circled the right one. Then turn the knob.
hint.ada.kitchen: The hatch is too high. There's something in the kitchen that could help.
hint.ada.photo: Look at the photo in the living room, and the calendar here in the kitchen: they tell you where they sat and which cups were theirs.
hint.ada.table: Put only their cups on the table: his chipped one by the window, the wisteria one by the stove. The teapot in the middle, the sugar bowl on his side.
hint.ada.crutch: The pantry has opened. Take what's inside.
hint.ada.hatch: Use the crutch to pull the hatch cord in the living room.
hint.ada.crates: Drag the crates away from the trunk.
hint.ada.code: The note in the hem: the day Ettore came back, 27 March. 2703.
hint.ada.take: Take the glasses. And don't turn around.
hint.ada.leave: Get out of this house. Take them to the Emporium.
emp.haveGlasses: Mrs Ada's glasses. She saw so well with them...
emp.feelGlasses: I can smell cold tea. Have you brought them to me?
emp.placedAda1: She didn't want to forget. I only gave her a way to remember.
emp.placedAda2: Two. You're getting good, boy. Almost as good as your sister.
emp.placedAda3: Lisa wasn't good. She was just brave.
emp.afterAda1: The village is waking up, object by object.
emp.afterAda2: But not every sleeper wants to be woken.
mem.ada.title: Memory — Ada and Ettore
mem.ada.1: 14 June 1946. Ettore comes home from the war on a crutch and marries Ada on the church steps. "I'll look at you as I did on the first day. Forever."
mem.ada.2: For twenty-five years, every evening: him by the window, her by the stove, the teapot between them. Then the television, and the rocking chair.
mem.ada.3: In 1971 the rocking chair is left empty. Ada keeps laying the table for two.
mem.ada.4: In 1974 a stranger dressed in black offers her a pair of round glasses. "You'll see better with these, madam. You'll see everything you've lost."
mem.ada.5: With the glasses Ettore came back to his chair, but he couldn't leave while she was looking. Ada locked them in the trunk, and every night she climbed back to the attic. Now he can go.
diary.memAda.title: Memory: Ada and Ettore
diary.memAda.text:
14 June 1946: Ettore comes home from the war on a crutch and marries Ada.
Every evening: him by the window, her by the stove, the teapot between them.
1971: Ettore dies. Ada keeps laying the table for two.
1974: the man in black sells her a pair of round glasses. "You'll see everything you've lost."
With the glasses Ettore is back in the rocking chair, but he can't leave while she's looking.
Ada locks the glasses in the trunk, but every night she climbs back to the attic. That's where they find her.
hint.map.choose: The Silver Mirror, Wisteria Cottage, The Stopped Hour or The Last Shot, Diego. You choose where to start.
hint.emporio.next: You've brought some back. The others are waiting: the Silver Mirror, Wisteria Cottage, the Stopped Hour, the Last Shot.
emp.placedBar: Aldo wanted his years back. I only sold them to him.
map.oraLocked: The Stopped Hour. Dozens of clocks in the window. All stopped. Not yet.
map.oraDone: A thick, steady ticking comes from The Stopped Hour. At last.
hint.map.ora: The Stopped Hour, Diego. The clockmaker's. Time doesn't pass in there.
hint.map.returnWatch: Take the watch to the Emporium, before it stops again.
emp.haveWatch: Ah, Ottavio's watch. For him a quarter past three was the loveliest hour in the world.
emp.placedOra: Ottavio wanted to stop time. I only showed him how.
emp.placed3a: Three. The village is starting to breathe, and I'm starting to feel cramped.
emp.placed3b: But remember, boy: every thing you bring back, someone once wanted.
emp.placed3c: Yes. And someone paid for it.
ora.enter1: L'Ora Ferma. Dozens of clocks, all stopped. Such silence... no. Under the silence there's something.
ora.enter2: A distant, dull thump-thump. A heart. Where is it coming from?
ora.clocks: All stopped. Ottavio didn't want to hear them.
ora.clocksAfter: Now they all tick together. It sounds like breathing.
ora.gf: A grandfather clock up to the ceiling. Its pendulum has been tied up with string.
ora.gfAfter: The pendulum swings back and forth. The sound fills the shop.
ora.case: Pocket watches lying open in the case, like shells. All stopped.
ora.tickets:
No. 301 — Mr Conti, alarm clock.
Too fast, it hammered against the ribs. Stopped. It no longer beats.

No. 302 — Mrs Bassi, kitchen clock.
Irregular, it limped at every breath. Too tiring to listen to. Silence.

No. 303 — Fernando the baker, turnip watch.
Heavy and tired, it seemed to want to give up on its own. I helped it stop.

No. 304 — the postman, wristwatch.
Breathless, it raced like a gear gone mad. Blocked. Quiet at last.

No. 305 — the widow Rinaldi, bedside clock.
Weak, barely a thread. It didn't deserve to go on disturbing the air.

No. 306 — Galli the schoolmaster, pocket watch.
Calm at first, then it began to beat too loud in the silence of the room. Silenced.

No. 307 — a boy passing through, no watch.
Too alive, too loud. I stopped it before it drove me mad.
ora.mantel: A mantel clock, stopped. Something rattles inside, stuck.
ora.shakeText: Shake the phone to shake the clock.
ora.mantelOpen: The little back door sprang open: there's a key inside.
ora.mantelAfter: The mantel clock. Its little door is open.
ora.keyTaken: A brass key with a tag: "Workshop".
ora.labOpen: The door opens. A smell of oil and metal.
ora.stairsOpen: The door opens. The stairs climb into the dark. Nothing can be heard, not even my steps.
ora.lab1: Ottavio's workshop. On the bench, an open movement. And a stethoscope, like a doctor's.
ora.movement: An open movement: the mainspring barrel on the left, the hand pinion on the right. In between, three empty arbors. There's something on the plate under the dust.
ora.movement2: Three empty arbors between the barrel and the pinion. The plate says how to fill them. And the big wheel... where has it gone?
ora.movementAfter: The wheels turn. The hand moves.
ora.plateDusty: A brass plate under a crust of dust. Something is engraved on it.
ora.blowText: Blow into the microphone to clear the dust.
ora.plateRead: "S · L · M": small, large, medium. The order of the three wheels, from the left.
ora.gearsWrong: The wheels jam. That's not the right order.
ora.gearsWrongX: The steel one doesn't belong: its teeth are different.
ora.drawerShut: A drawer under the bench. It won't open: it only springs when the movement turns.
ora.drawerOpen: The movement turns and the drawer under the bench springs open.
ora.photoTitle: On the back of the photo
ora.photoBack:
Clara Sala, my little girl.
9 December 1961.
The happiest day.
— Dad (Ottavio Sala, clockmaker)
ora.windKey: And a winding key, big, with a crank. For an enormous clock.
ora.shelves: Clocks in pieces, waiting. On each a tag: «Stopped».
ora.apron: Ottavio's apron. In the pocket, balls of cotton wool for the ears.
ora.cam1: The walls are padded. All of them. The door too. Sound dies in here as soon as it's born.
ora.cam2: And there's someone on the bed. An old man, on his back, hands folded on his chest. He seems to be asleep.
ora.bed: A brass bed. Under the blanket, the shape of a little girl.
ora.claraLook: Clara. Her eyes are open, staring at the ceiling. She isn't breathing, but she isn't dead.
ora.shoutText: Call him: «Ottavio!». Speak loudly into the microphone.
ora.clara1: Daddy stopped time... so that I wouldn't go.
ora.clara2: But I can't stay, and I can't go. It's so cold...
ora.clara3: It's up there. In the tower. Make it start again... please.
ora.towerOpen: The little door to the tower has opened by itself.
ora.towerLocked: A low little door, padded too. It won't open. As if someone were holding it from the other side.
ora.nightstand: A music box and a glass of water. The water is as still as glass.
ora.nightstandAfter: The music box plays by itself now. Softly.
ora.dust: I reach out: the dust doesn't move. It's as still as if it were painted on the air.
ora.dustAfter: The dust drifts down, slowly, like snow.
ora.claraGone: The bed is empty. On the pillow, only a little grey dust.
ora.camAfter: The dust is moving. And the bed... Clara isn't there any more.
ora.tower1: The clock tower. Wheels, chains, weights. The dial seen from behind, back to front.
ora.tower2: Everything still. The weights are on the floor. And between the wheels... something red.
ora.movementStill: An enormous movement, stopped. The weights have run down to the floor.
ora.movementRuns: The movement turns, slow and heavy. Every tick shakes the floor.
ora.watchSeen: A red pocket watch, jammed between two wheels. While it's there, nothing can turn.
ora.watchStuck: It's jammed. The movement has to turn to free it.
ora.watchTaken: Ottavio's watch. I hold it to my ear... and I hear my own heart. Deafening. I pull it away at once.
ora.socket: A square arbor on the weight drum. It needs a winding key.
ora.keyIn: The key fits the arbor. Now I have to turn it.
ora.turnKey: Turn the crank: finger on the key, in circles.
ora.woundDone: The weights are up. The movement is wound.
ora.wedge: A wooden wedge jammed under the pendulum. If I pull it now, unwound, nothing will happen.
ora.wedgePull: The wedge is holding the pendulum. Drag it away.
ora.runningNow: The movement runs on its own now.
ora.restarted1: The pendulum swings. The wheels turn. And for a moment, beneath me, the whole village beats: hearts, clocks, all together.
ora.restarted2: Then only the tick-tock of the tower. And something red has fallen from the wheels.
ora.dial: The tower dial, seen from behind. The hands are enormous.
note.gears: Workshop: gears in the order S · L · M (small, large, medium).
note.clara: Clara Sala, Ottavio the clockmaker's daughter, was born on 9 December 1961.
hint.ora.shake: Now that it's quiet: the mantel clock on the counter. Shake it.
hint.ora.key: The mantel clock's little door is open. Take the key.
hint.ora.labdoor: Use the key on the workshop door, behind the counter.
hint.ora.lab: In the workshop, Diego. The movement on the bench: the drawer holds what the metronome is missing.
hint.ora.blow: The plate on the bench is covered in dust. Blow on it.
hint.ora.gears: Drag the wheels onto the arbors: small, large, medium. The steel one isn't needed.
hint.ora.drawer: The drawer under the bench has opened. Take what's inside.
hint.ora.code: The stairs have a four-digit lock. The date on Clara's photo: day and month.
hint.ora.upstairs: Go up, Diego. He's up there.
hint.ora.call: Call him, Diego. Loudly. Even if he's asleep. Even if he doesn't want you to.
hint.ora.tower: The little tower door is open.
hint.ora.needKey: You need the winding key from the workshop.
hint.ora.socket: Put the winding key in the square arbor of the drum.
hint.ora.wind: Turn the key until the weights are at the top.
hint.ora.wedge: Pull out the wedge that's holding the pendulum.
hint.ora.takeWatch: Something red fell. Pick it up.
hint.ora.leave: Take it to the Emporium, Diego.
mem.ora.title: Memory — Ottavio Sala
mem.ora.1: Ottavio Sala has mended clocks since 1948. He can hear the heart of a movement before he even opens it.
mem.ora.2: Then the world begins to go quiet. Ottavio puts his ear to the gears, and hears nothing any more.
mem.ora.3: One night a stranger dressed in black comes in. He offers him a pocket watch. «You'll hear everything again.»
mem.ora.4: Ottavio hears again. Then he hears too much: the hearts of customers, neighbours, passers-by. Thump-thump, day and night. To have peace, he stops them. One at a time.
mem.ora.5: In the silence of the padded room, the last thing he remembered was a lullaby. Now he has heard it again.
diary.memOra.title: Memory: Ottavio and Clara
diary.memOra.text:
Ottavio Sala, clockmaker since 1948. His daughter Clara, born on 9 December 1961, helps him in the shop.
1974: Clara falls ill.
The man in black sells him a pocket watch: "As long as the hands stay still, time won't take anything from her."
Ottavio stops it at 3:17. Every clock stops, and so does Clara: neither alive nor dead.
Time has started again. Clara has gone.
retro.yardKey: An iron key with a tag: "Courtyard".
retro.yardLocked: The back door. Locked. Through the frosted glass there's only rain.
retro.yardOpen: The door opens onto the courtyard. A smell of rain and wet stone.
hint.retro.yard: The key opens the back door, Diego. The one with the frosted glass.
hint.retro.goYard: Go out into the courtyard. The trapdoor crank isn't in here.
yard.enter1: The courtyard behind the shop. It's raining, and the sheets are still out on the line.
yard.enter2: A well. And stone steps going up to a door left ajar.
yard.well: A stone well. Down at the bottom there's a bucket on the rope. Something's in it.
yard.wellBucket: The bucket is up. There's a bundle of oilcloth in it.
yard.wellAfter: The water down there is black and still. Better not to look too long.
yard.padlock: A chain round the winch drum, closed with a padlock. Someone didn't want that bucket coming up.
yard.winchLocked: The winch handle won't turn: the chain is holding it.
yard.turnWinch: Turn the handle: finger on the grip, in circles. Three turns.
yard.unlocked: The padlock opens. The chain slides down, rattling.
yard.bucketUp: The bucket came up... and for a moment, in the water, there was a face.
yard.crank1: Wrapped in the oilcloth there's an iron crank.
yard.crank2: The trapdoor crank. Aldo hid it here, so that nobody would go down to the cellar.
yard.gate: The gate to the alley. Shut with a chain and a rusty padlock.
yard.sheets: Sheets hung out who knows how long ago. They never dry. One has a stain that looks like a face.
hint.yard.aldo: The padlock on the well... The key must be at Aldo's, up the stairs.
hint.yard.padlock: You've got the padlock key. Use it on the winch chain.
hint.yard.winch: Turn the winch handle and bring up the bucket.
hint.yard.bucket: There's something in the bucket. Take it.
hint.yard.back: Back to the back room, Diego. The crank goes in the trapdoor.
aldo.enter1: Aldo's lodging, over the shop. A soldier's bed, everything in order.
aldo.enter2: The mirror over the washstand is covered with a cloth. And on that wall... it's him, every time.
aldo.portraits1: Portraits of Aldo. 1951, 1962, 1973: he gets older, like everyone.
aldo.portraits2: Then October 1974, November 1974... and he goes backwards. In November he looks like a boy.
aldo.portraits3: The last one, December 1974: the chair is empty.
aldo.cloth: A cloth nailed over the mirror. Aldo didn't want to see himself.
aldo.mirror: It was him. In the mirror. Behind me.
aldo.mirrorAfter: The mirror is uncovered. Now there's only me in it. I think.
aldo.wash: A basin and a jug. A film of dust on the water.
aldo.table: Aldo's table. An oil lamp, a letter, a piggy bank.
aldo.letter:
Dear brother,
I don't know who else to write to. Every man I shave gets up from the chair older, and I younger. I can see it in the portraits, year after year.
I've shut the cellar. What opens it I've given back to the water: let it keep it, down in the dark, where the rope no longer reaches.
And the iron that holds the rope fast I've put to sleep with the money that is never spent.
The chair is down there. Nobody must ever sit in it again.
— Aldo
note.well: Aldo's letter: "what opens the cellar I've given back to the water". And "the iron that holds the rope fast" sleeps "with the money that is never spent".
aldo.pig: An earthenware piggy bank. Something metal rattles inside.
aldo.shakeText: Shake the phone to shake the piggy bank.
aldo.keyOut: A small key has slid out of the slot.
aldo.keyTaken: A little padlock key. The one for the well.
aldo.pigEmpty: The piggy bank is empty now. It doesn't rattle any more.
aldo.bed: The bed is made with the sheets pulled tight as a drum. Nobody has slept in it for years.
aldo.wardrobe: White barber's coats in a row. Each one a little smaller than the last. The last would fit a boy.
hint.aldo.letter: There's a letter on the table. Read it.
hint.aldo.pig: The piggy bank on the table. Shake it.
hint.aldo.take: The little key is on the table. Take it.
hint.aldo.leave: Back down to the courtyard, Diego. The padlock is on the well.
ada.shedKey: A key with a handwritten tag: "shed".
ada.gardenOpen: The kitchen door opens onto the garden. The wisteria has taken over everything.
hint.ada.shedKey: There's a key in the pantry. Take it.
hint.ada.garden: The shed key, Diego. The shed is in the garden: through the kitchen door.
garden.enter1: The garden behind the cottage. The wisteria has covered the pergola, the wall... everything.
garden.enter2: A swing is moving. There's no wind.
garden.window: A French window, buried under the wisteria. There's a bedroom behind it. No way through: it needs cutting.
garden.wisteria: The wisteria. Its trunk is as thick as an arm. Who knows how old it is.
garden.shedOpen: The shed opens. A rake, a spade, a tin box... and an empty nail.
garden.shedInside: Ettore's tools, neatly kept. The nail for the shears is empty.
garden.shedEmpty: Ettore's tools. Nobody has touched them in years.
garden.cut1: The wisteria comes down in clumps. Behind it, the French window.
garden.cut2: On the glass, from the inside... handprints.
garden.swing: The swing goes back and forth, slowly. As if someone had just got off.
garden.birdbath: A birdbath full of black rainwater. No birds here.
hint.garden.shed: The shed, on the right. Use the key.
hint.garden.shears: The shears are in the shed. Take them.
hint.garden.cut: Use the shears on the wisteria over the French window.
hint.garden.bedroom: The French window is clear. Go in.
ac.enter1: Ada's bedroom. The double bed is made on one side only.
ac.enter2: On the other side the blanket is turned down. As every evening, for someone who never comes back.
ac.bed: On her side, the dent of a head in the pillow. On the other, nothing. For years.
ac.samplerRead: An embroidered sampler over the bed: "Till death us do part". And their wedding date.
ac.dresser: Ada's dressing table. An oval mirror, a hairbrush, a music box.
ac.mirrorAfter: There's only the room in the mirror. Now.
ac.musicbox: A lacquered music box with a dancer under a glass dome. The winding key is at the front.
ac.playing: The music starts. The dancer turns...
ac.afterScare: It was her. In the mirror. Over my shoulder.
ac.drawerOpen: When the music ended, a little drawer opened in the base of the music box.
ac.keyTaken: A little brass key. The wardrobe's, surely.
ac.boxAfter: The music box is silent. The little drawer is empty.
ac.wardOpen1: The wardrobe opens. Inside, a man's suit, carefully hung. It still smells of tobacco.
ac.wardOpen2: Leaning at the back, a crutch. And on the shelf, Ada's work basket.
ac.crutch: Ettore's crutch. He came back from the war like that.
ac.wardEmpty: Ettore's suit. The sleeve stirs, as if someone had just let go of it.
ac.hallDoor: The door to the hall. Locked from the other side.
hint.ac.musicbox: The music box on the dressing table, Diego. Wind it up.
hint.ac.key: There's a key in the music box drawer.
hint.ac.crutch: In the wardrobe: Ettore's crutch and Ada's work basket. Take everything.
note.cups: Calendar: Ettore's cup is the chipped one. Ada's has wisteria on it.
ada.pieceE: A white cup with a chipped rim and a thin crack.
ada.pieceA: A cup painted all round with little hanging clusters of flowers. Wisteria.
ada.pieceX: A cup with dark stripes. A different set.
ada.pieceY: A plain white cup, not a scratch on it. Never used.
ada.pieceS: The sugar bowl, with its lid. Full to the brim.
ada.wrongSugar: The sugar bowl stood on his side. He was the one with the sweet tooth.
emp.story.shoe1: A slipper of Marie-Madeleine d'Aubray, Marquise de Brinvilliers. Paris, 1676.
emp.story.shoe2: She poisoned her father and her brothers with a little powder, a spoonful at a time. They called it "inheritance powder". She wanted that inheritance so badly.
emp.story.shoe3: Did she bring it here herself? Or did someone bring it back?
emp.story.statue1: Erzsébet Báthory. A countess, Hungary, sixteen hundreds. That statuette stood on her dressing table.
emp.story.statue2: She wanted to stay young forever. They say it took the girls of the village to manage it. A great many girls.
emp.story.statue3: I don't want to know how he got it.
emp.story.doll1: Amelia Dyer's doll. England, the end of the eighteen hundreds. She took in babies, for a fee.
emp.story.doll2: The mothers paid and went home easy. The babies... ended up in the Thames. The money was all she wanted.
emp.story.doll3: It has glass eyes. And they follow me.
emp.story.macelleria1: A group of young people brought this back to me last year. Then another group. And another.
emp.story.macelleria2: Every time they bring it back, and every time Bruno takes it again. It's never really over, down there.
emp.story.macelleria3: My father's butcher's shop. I don't want to look under that cloth.
emp.story.valigia1: The suitcase maker sold journeys to people who couldn't leave. You only had to open the case and dream.
emp.story.valigia2: Then the dreams stopped ending. He stayed inside. Some suitcases won't close any more.
emp.story.valigia3: It's tied with a red knot. It looks tied from the inside.
emp.story.razor1: Aldo's razor. A year for every shave: he took them off his customers and put them on himself.
emp.story.razor2: He asked me for it, you know. He wanted to be the boy cutting hair in the square again.
emp.story.razor3: And in the end he vanished altogether. Like in that last photo.
emp.story.glasses1: Ada's glasses. With these she could still see Ettore, sitting by the window.
emp.story.glasses2: She didn't want him to go. And he, kind man, stayed. Twenty-eight years.
emp.story.glasses3: Now he can leave. I hope.
emp.story.watch1: Ottavio's watch. Stopped at seventeen minutes past three, the hour Clara fell asleep.
emp.story.watch2: A father would do anything. I only gave him the means.
emp.story.watch3: Now the hands are moving. And Clara is free.
ora.envelope1: An envelope waiting to be collected: "Morandi — wall clock". Inside there's a minute hand, straightened.
ora.envelope2: Morandi... Aldo Morandi, the barber. The hand off his clock.
ora.trayMissing: There's an empty space in the tray, with a tag: "Big wheel — lent to Ettore, at Wisteria Cottage".
ora.gearBack: The big wheel goes back in its place in the tray. Now they're all here.
hint.ora.needGear: The big wheel is missing: the tag says Ottavio lent it to Ettore, at Wisteria Cottage.
hint.ora.gearBack: You've got the big wheel. Put it in the tray on the workshop bench.
cantina.noHand: The clock has no minute hand. On the dial, a note: "Taken to Sala, the clockmaker".
cantina.handOn: The hand clicks onto the arbor. Now the clock can be set.
hint.cantina.noHand: The minute hand is missing. Aldo took it to the clockmaker's: The Stopped Hour.
hint.cantina.handOn: You've got the hand: put it on the clock.
garden.nail: An empty nail. Under it, in pencil: "shears — lent to Aldo, the barber".
garden.tin1: A tin full of screws, springs, washers. Ettore fixed everything.
garden.tin2: And in among them, a big brass cogwheel. It's engraved: "O. Sala".
hint.garden.tin: There's something in the tin in the shed that isn't Ettore's.
hint.garden.shearsAway: The shears aren't here: Ettore lent them to Aldo, the barber. Look for them at The Silver Mirror.
yard.shears1: Pruning shears, hanging on a nail. The tag says: "Bassi — to return".
yard.shears2: Ettore Bassi. Ada's husband. I'll take them back to him.
map.fotoLocked: The Last Shot. Portraits of village people in the window. Not yet.
map.fotoDone: The portraits have gone from the photographer's window. Only empty backdrops. And people in the street.
hint.map.foto: The Last Shot, Diego. The photographer's. The village people disappear, and his photos stay.
hint.map.returnCamera: Take the camera to the Emporium.
emp.haveCamera: Ferri's camera. His photos never faded, did you know? I promised him that.
emp.placedFoto: Giulio wanted his photos never to fade. And they didn't: the people did.
emp.placed4a: Four. I'm starting to feel the cold, boy.
emp.placed4b: But there are more still out there. And Bruno... Bruno doesn't forget.
emp.placed4c: Then I'll come back. As many times as it takes.
emp.story.camera1: Giulio Ferri's camera. He'd photographed the village for thirty years.
emp.story.camera2: He asked me that his photos should never fade. He asked nothing about the people.
emp.story.camera3: And whoever stood in front of the lens stayed in there. Perfect.
ada.redbulb1: In the suitcase, with the letters, a box of spare bulbs. One is red, for a darkroom.
ada.redbulb2: The label says: "Ferri — to return". Ettore borrowed everything.
foto.enter1: The Last Shot. Ferri took everyone's communion photo, wedding photo... and funeral photo.
foto.enter2: Half the village is on that wall. People I haven't seen around for weeks.
foto.wall1: The Rinaldis. Father Pietro. The mayor. Granny Tilde... all posing, pin-sharp.
foto.wall2: They searched for Granny Tilde for days. Nobody's seen the mayor since November. And here they're perfect, as if just printed.
foto.wall3: Perfect portraits. Not one of them is still in the village.
foto.wallAfter: Now the frames hold only empty backdrops. Outside, I can hear voices.
foto.cameras: Cameras in the display. A Leica, a Rolleiflex. Nothing red here.

note.lastra: Ledger: 14 December, Giulio Ferri took a self-portrait. The plate number is inked out.
foto.stairsLocked: The door up to the flat. "Private". Locked.
foto.stairsOpen: The door opens. The stairs go up into the dark.
foto.studio1: The studio. The painted backdrop, the chair, the lamps. And the camera on its tripod, under the black cloth.
foto.studio2: It looks as if it's waiting for someone to photograph.
foto.chair: The posing chair. On the cushion, the dent of someone who has just stood up.
foto.chairAfter: The chair is empty. Really empty, now.
foto.backdrop: The backdrop: painted clouds and a fake balustrade. I can't see anything odd. With the naked eye.
foto.lens1: Under the black cloth, the ground glass. The picture is upside down, as always... and out of focus.
foto.lens2: There's something on the backdrop, but it's all blurred. I need to focus: the brass wheel.
foto.lensBlur: Out of focus. Turn the brass wheel beside the glass to focus.
foto.lensSharp: In focus. On the backdrop, those numbers you can't see with the naked eye.
foto.sharp1: Now I can see it. On the empty backdrop, in the glass, numbers appear that aren't in the room.
note.darkcode: Through the lens, on the backdrop: 2 7 0 4.
foto.darkOpen: The darkroom door opens. A smell of acid. Pitch black.
foto.dark1: The darkroom. I can't see a thing.
foto.dark2: White light would ruin the paper. I'd need the red lamp.
foto.noBulb: The safelight. It's empty: no bulb. Under it, a note.
foto.lentNote: red bulb: lent to E. Bassi
foto.red1: Red light fills the room. The trays, the bottles, the paper under the enlarger.
foto.red2: There's already a picture on the paper, invisible: it needs developing.
foto.redOn: The red light. The only colour I've seen since I came to the village.
foto.tooDark: Too dark to read. I need the red light.
foto.benchDark: The bench. I can't work in the dark.
foto.bench: Three trays, each with a sign: a square, a triangle, a circle. And the sheet to develop.
foto.benchGoing: The sheet is halfway through the baths. Go on, in the right order.
foto.benchDone: The print is hanging up to dry.
foto.bottles: Three bottles: Developer with the triangle, Stop bath with the circle, Fixer with the square.
foto.chartRead: Developer first, rocking the tray. Then the stop bath. Then the fixer.
note.baths: Darkroom: developer (rock it), then stop bath, then fixer. The bottles show each bath's sign.
foto.shakeText: Shake the phone to rock the tray.
foto.devDone: The picture comes up out of nothing. Now the stop bath.
foto.wrongFirst: The paper goes black all over. Ruined. Luckily there's another exposed sheet in the box.
foto.wrongBath: Wrong bath: the print is spoilt. I'll start again with another sheet.
foto.print1: The print is dry. It's the archive cabinet: lots of little drawers. One is white, and a pale hand points at it.
foto.print2: Fourth row from the top, seventh drawer. Thirty-one. Like the plate in the order book.
note.drawer: The print: in the archive, drawer 31 (fourth row, seventh from the left).
foto.arch1: The archive. Thirty years of plates and negatives. The whole village is in here.
foto.cabinet: A cabinet of forty numbered little drawers. Plates, negatives.
foto.drawerB: Negatives of children posing on the rocking horse.
foto.drawerD: First communions. White dresses, black faces: negatives are always frightening.
foto.drawer13: Thirteen. A single plate: an empty room. In the middle, a shadow standing, looking at me.
foto.d31a: Thirty-one. A plate: a man sitting, waistcoat, looking straight into the lens. Giulio Ferri.
foto.d31b: Under the plate, a little tin with a letter lock. Something rattles inside: a key.
foto.keyTaken: The key to the flat upstairs.
foto.lightbox: A light table. On it, a negative: a family posing. Instead of faces, white blotches.
foto.flat1: Ferri's flat. It smells of tobacco and acid.
foto.flat2: There's someone at the table. You can see the chair through him.
foto.giulio1: Have you come for your portrait? I'm sorry. I don't work any more.
foto.giulio2: I only wanted my photos never to fade. I watched them go yellow, one after another... He gave me that camera.
foto.giulio3: And the people of the village ended up in there.
foto.giulio4: All of them. And on the fourteenth I took the last one: mine.
foto.giulio5: There's only one way. A photo with the flash, with the last magnesium bulb. The flash lets them out.
foto.giulio6: Take my last picture, boy. Down there, in the studio. I'll wait for you by the chair.
foto.giulio7: The bulb is on the table. Take it.
foto.giulio8: I'll wait for you in the studio. By the chair. Get me in focus.
foto.bulbOnTable: On the table, where there was nothing before, there's a magnesium flash bulb.
foto.bulbTaken: A magnesium flash bulb. It works only once.
foto.table: The light table, tilted. Here Giulio retouched the negatives. It's empty now.
foto.self: The self-portrait of 14 December. Perfect, sharp. He himself can barely be seen.
foto.selfAfter: The self-portrait. Now the frame holds only the empty chair.
foto.shelf: Boxes of blank plates and magnesium bulbs. All empty.
foto.bulbNotYet: I have to get him in focus first. The brass wheel.
foto.lastReady: He's there, in focus, by the chair. Looking at me. The bulb is loaded.
foto.shoutText: Shout "Hold still!" into the phone to take the picture.
foto.freed1: The flash. And for a moment the studio is full of people: everyone from the portraits.
foto.freed2: Then nothing. Only the camera, red as embers. Now it can be touched.
foto.taken1: The bellows camera. It's warm, like something alive.
hint.foto.register: The order book on the counter, Diego. Look at the last line.
hint.foto.studio: In the studio, the camera under the black cloth. Look into the glass.
hint.foto.cloth: Take the black cloth off the camera.

mem.foto.title: Memory — Giulio Ferri
mem.foto.1: Giulio Ferri has photographed Rocca del Castello for thirty years: christenings, weddings, the dead in their coffins. He knows every face in the village.
mem.foto.2: But his photos yellow, fade, get lost. Giulio can't bear it: it's as if the village were vanishing with them.
mem.foto.3: One evening a stranger dressed in black walks in and puts a bellows camera on the counter. "Your photos will never fade."
mem.foto.4: It's true. The photos stay perfect. It's the people who vanish: whoever stands before the lens stays inside the plate.
mem.foto.5: The flash of the last bulb opened the plates. The village has come home. And Giulio, at last, has faded.
diary.memFoto.title: Memory: Giulio Ferri
diary.memFoto.text:
Giulio Ferri, photographer, has portrayed the village for thirty years.
He can't bear his photos fading.
The man in black sells him a bellows camera: "Your photos will never fade."
The photos stay perfect; it's the people who vanish, shut in the plates.
On 14 December Giulio takes his own portrait.
The flash of the last magnesium bulb set everyone free.

No. 86 — Mrs Conti — Phonola radio: output valve replaced. Ready.
No. 87 — Parish — bell amplifier: done. I keep the bell-tower key until they pay.
No. 88 — G. Ferri (photographer) — lent him the spare ECC83 from MY station, for his enlarger timer. Says he keeps it in the archive, drawer 17. Get it back!!
No. 89 — Morandi (barber) — transistor radio: nothing to be done.
No. 90 — ...
(the last one is written crooked, in pencil)

radio.tvsOff: Three TV sets stacked up. Grey screens, dead.
radio.tvsOn: Snow. On all three. Nobody turned them on.
radio.tvFace1: A face. A man with headphones on. He was looking at me.
radio.tvFace2: The same as in the photo on the wall. Nello.

radio.photo2: On the back, in pencil: «1972. The year before the voices».
radio.padlockNo: Three digits. Nello locked his own room. Who was he hiding from?

radio.box1: The fuse box. Six fuses, and one is missing: the one marked MAIN — 10 A.
radio.box2: The spares are on the shelf on the right. I'll test them on the lamp first: a blown fuse is no use.

radio.slotEmpty: The empty MAIN slot, 10 A. I need a good 10 A: the spares are on the shelf on the right.

radio.powerOn: The bulb flickers and stays on. There's power all over the house.

radio.cellarVoice2: Voices. Many, all together, muffled. As if they came from behind the walls.
radio.labEnter: Nello's lab. The soldering iron is still in its stand. As if he had just stepped out.
radio.labEnterDark: The workshop. Without light I can hardly see. A reel-to-reel tape recorder, on the bench.
radio.schema: The diagram of Nello's station. Two ECC83 valves, and one has a red pencil circle: «AT FERRI'S».
radio.benchPhoto: Nello at his bench. Focused, calm. Before.
radio.bench: Valves, resistors, a cold soldering iron. And dust on everything, except the tape recorder.
radio.calendar: June 1973. The 12th is circled over and over, with «THE FIRST VOICE» written by it. After that the calendar was never turned.
radio.tapeNoPower: A Geloso tape recorder. No power, no spin.

radio.tapeAfter2: He recorded it like that on purpose, so nobody would understand. If I turn the reel by hand, the other way...

radio.tapeBack2: «I go out onto the roof from my bedroom window. I lock the room with the day of the first voice: one, two, six. The twelfth of June.»
radio.tapeBack3: «Nobody must touch the station. Nobody. Over and out.»

radio.roomEnter2: On the wall over the bed, pencil circles. Lots of them.

1  · — — — —      6  — · · · ·
2  · · — — —      7  — — · · ·
3  · · · — —      8  — — — · ·
4  · · · · —      9  — — — — ·

radio.bed: Nello's bed, against the neighbours' wall. The sheets pulled up over the pillow, as if not to hear.

radio.terrace2: Nello's antenna. And his station, in the shack.

radio.faint3: The voice comes and goes. The antenna points at the village, sideways. It wants me to look up.

radio.rxAfter: The receiver is off. Only a ticking, as the valve cools.

radio.mastDone: The antenna points straight at the sky. Better not touch it.
radio.antNothing: The antenna points at the sky. But the station picks up nothing: I have to tune it first.
radio.tower: The bell tower. From up here it looks small.
radio.contact1: «SARTORI. YOU HAVE BEEN LOOKING FOR ME A LONG TIME.»
radio.contact2: «I hear you... at last I hear you. I've listened to everyone in the village. Every word, every secret. Only you were missing.»
radio.contact3: «AND NOW THAT YOU HEAR ME, YOU WILL NEVER STOP. NO ONE STOPS, AFTER ME. KEEP LISTENING, SARTORI. FOR EVER.»
radio.contact4: «For ever... I haven't slept in a year. The voices don't stop, not even switched off. Not even dead.»
radio.contact6: «Boy... the key. My hand won't obey me any more. You close it. Once and for all, so I can rest.»

radio.keyNo: Not like that. The notebook says: all run together, at the end.
radio.keyAfter: The key is still. There's nothing more to say.
radio.free3: The chair is empty. The receiver switches itself off, slowly.
radio.free4: Only the red transistor is still on. With no batteries.
radio.radiolina: A red transistor radio. Switched on. The battery compartment is empty.
radio.radiolinaContact: The little radio whispers with a thousand voices at once. The whole village, and under it, that bigger voice.
radio.taken1: The man in black's radio. It goes dead the moment I pick it up.
radio.taken2: It's heavier than it should be.
radio.towerKey: In the battery compartment there's a long key with a tag: «BELL TOWER — amplifier. Parish». I keep it.

emp.story.radio2: Every night it spoke to him in his son's voice. And every night Nello lost a little more.
emp.story.radio3: And in the end he closed it himself. With the key, the way the boy taught him.
emp.placed5b: The Suitcase, boy. Your sister's. And Bruno knows you're coming.
mem.radio.title: Memory — Nello Sartori
mem.radio.1: Nello Sartori mends radios and televisions. He has the finest ear in the village: he hears a wrong hum before he even switches on.
mem.radio.2: On 12 June 1973, interference: in the radio on the bench are the Contis, the neighbours, arguing. Nello stays listening until night.
mem.radio.3: One evening a stranger dressed in black comes in and sets a red transistor on the counter. «With this you will hear everyone. Truly everyone.»
mem.radio.4: It's true. The barber, the watchmaker, the photographer, the widow of the wisteria. Every secret in the village. But Nello wants more: the voice above all voices.
mem.radio.5: On the roof, the Supreme Voice answered him, and would not let him go. Diego keyed «end of transmission». And up there, at last, there is silence.
diary.memRadio.title: Memory: Nello Sartori
diary.memRadio.text:
Nello Sartori, radio repairman, the finest ear in the village.
On 12 June 1973 interference lets him hear the neighbours. From that day he wants to hear everyone.
The man in black sells him a red transistor: «You will hear everyone. Truly everyone.»
With it he hears every secret in the village. Then he looks for the voice above them all: the Supreme Voice.
On the roof he found it, and it would not let him go.
I keyed «end of transmission» for him. Now he rests.
In the little radio was the bell-tower key.

diary.lisaUv.title: Lisa's messages
diary.lisaUv.text:
Five messages in invisible ink, one in each shop, signed L.
They say that day at the butcher's I was there.
That dad was looking for me, and I was hiding.
That the man in black took my memories.
And to remember the 24th.
The rest is in the church.

emp.hourglass1: The hourglass. Turn it over, boy. Let's see how much you have left.
emp.hourglassText: Turn the phone over, as if you were turning the hourglass.
emp.hourglass2: The sand always comes back down. So do memories, sooner or later.
emp.hourglass3: He knows what I've forgotten. I'm sure of it.

ch.diary:
23 October 1974

Dad isn't himself anymore. The stranger says: «I only sold him what he wanted».
Tomorrow I'll talk to him, in the shop. Diego is coming with me, he won't leave me alone.
If something happens, Diego, it isn't your fault.
Don't forget me.

L.
mem.diego.title: Memory — Diego
mem.diego.1: 24 October 1974. The butcher's. Lisa and I come in from the back: dad is in the shop, but he doesn't look at us.
mem.diego.2: Then he sees us. He has the cleaver in his hand, and someone else's eyes. Lisa pushes me into the cold room and shuts the door.
mem.diego.3: Cold. Dark. From outside, Lisa screaming my name. Then nothing.
mem.diego.4: When the door opens, there's a man dressed in black. «I can make you forget, boy. All of it.»
mem.diego.5: «In return, you'll bring my things back to me. One by one.» I said yes. And I forgot.
diary.memDiego.title: Memory: Diego
diary.memDiego.text:
24 October 1974: I was at the butcher's with Lisa.
Dad, with the cleaver, wasn't himself.
Lisa hid me in the cold room.
The man in black offered to make me forget everything.
In return: bring his things back to him.
I accepted. And now I remember.
ch.lisa2: Lisa... I'm sorry. I made a deal with him.
ch.lisa3: I know. Come and get me, Diego. I'm in the suitcase.

m2card.1:
You remember the 24th of October.
And now you know who is waiting, at the end of the square.
m2card.2:
From the Premiata Macelleria comes a dull thud.
Then another. Dad is calling you.
m2.enter1: Now I remember it. The counter, the neon, the cold room. The 24th of October.
m2.enter2: Something's written on the back wall. My name.
m2.enter3: The cold room door is open. On the floor a dark smear runs from the cold room to the curing room door. And back.
m2.enter4: Dad is still here. I can't go to Lisa and leave him like this.
m2.counter1: The counter is just as before. The fingers, the hand, the price cards.
m2.counter2: Only now I know what the «deliveries DOWNSTAIRS» were.
m2.ledger:
Tuesday — 2 kg rib, Mrs Ada
Tuesday — delivery DOWNSTAIRS
Tuesday — delivery DOWNSTAIRS
14 October — The favour is paid.
24 October — delivery DOWNSTAIRS — 3.7 kg

⟦Diego, Dad locked the curing room key in the scale.
The drawer under the pan only opens at the right weight:
the weight of the last delivery.
— L.⟧
m2.ledgerRead: Lisa's writing. The curing room key is in the scale: the drawer opens at the weight of the last delivery. 3.7 kilos.
note.m2.ledger: Ledger (Lisa's ink): the curing room key is in the scale drawer, which opens at the weight of the last delivery. Last line: 24 October, 3.7 kg.
m2.scale: The scale's needle trembles, as if something invisible were on the pan. Under the pan there's a locked drawer.
m2.scaleTitle: The scale: what should it read? (kg)
m2.scaleOpen: The needle stops at 3.7. Click: the drawer under the pan slides open. Inside, a key tagged «Curing room».
m2.scaleEmpty: The scale drawer is empty. The needle is back at zero.
m2.photo1: Our photo. Dad's face isn't scratched out any more.
m2.photo2: He's looking at me. Tired eyes, not cruel ones. What chased me wasn't him.
m2.hooks: On the second hook there's no pig any more. It's a torso. Human. I don't want to know whose.
m2.labLocked: The curing room door, under the stairs. Locked. Dad always kept it locked.
m2.labOpened: The lock turns. A smell of salt and cellar comes out of the curing room.
m2.labEnter1: The curing room. Dad spent his nights here.
m2.labEnter2: The hams sway. There's not a breath of air.
m2.grinder: Dad's meat grinder, clamped to the bench. When I shake it, something metal rattles inside.
m2.grinderHow: The crank: turn it with your finger. Lisa wrote «backwards»: anticlockwise.
m2.grinderWrong: The crank turns and the thing inside drops even lower. This way I'll only grind it.
m2.grinderWrong2: Backwards, Lisa wrote. The other way.
m2.grinderAlmost: Something rattles its way back up. A few more turns, backwards.
m2.grinderUvRead: Lisa: the cellar key is in the grinder. Turn the crank backwards. And it'll make noise.
uv.m2grinder1: The cellar key is in the grinder.
uv.m2grinder2: Turn it backwards. He'll hear. Put everything out. — L.
note.m2.grinder: Curing room (Lisa's ink): the cellar key is in the grinder. Turn the crank backwards (anticlockwise). It'll make noise: then put out the light and hide.
m2.bench: The workbench. Knives, string, a whetstone.
m2.keyOut: Three turns backwards and a greasy black key drops from the grinder's mouth. The cellar key.
m2.hide1: Footsteps. Heavy. From the shop. He heard me.
m2.hideText: Put the light out and don't move: lay the phone face down until he's gone.
m2.brunoSniff: ...Diego? I can hear you. I can smell you, son.
m2.hideOk: He's gone. He was a metre away. He didn't see me.
m2.hideFail: A huge hand grabs your shoulder. Then nothing: only cold, and footsteps going away.
m2.hideFail2: He let me go. As if, for a moment, he knew me.
m2.block1: The chopping block. The cleaver is buried in it up to the handle.
m2.block2: I try to pull it out. It won't move. As if someone were holding it down.
m2.saltTaken: The salt bin. I fill a little bag.
m2.trapLocked: A trapdoor in the floor, padlocked. The cellar.
m2.trapOpen: The padlock opens. Under the trapdoor, a wooden ladder goes down into the dark.
m2.hams: Hams and salami, hung to cure. At the back, among the hams, something else is hanging. I don't look.
m2.cellaLisa: Keep quiet, Diego. Whatever you hear. Don't come out.
m2.cellaEnter1: The door shut by itself. Like that day.
m2.cellaEnter2: It's open again. The cold room. In here I waited, in the dark, for hours.
m2.ice: There's a sheet of ice on the floor. Frozen inside it, a white ribbon. Lisa's hair ribbon.
m2.blowText: The ice is thin. Breathe on it, long, to melt it.
m2.iceMelted: The ice melts under your breath. The ribbon is free.
m2.iceMatches: A match isn't enough, in here it dies at once. It takes warm breath.
m2.iceEmpty: Just a puddle of icy water.
m2.ribbon1: Lisa's ribbon. She had it in her hair that day.
m2.ribbon2: She must have lost it when she pushed me in here.
m2.coat1: Dad's coat, on the hook. Stiff with cold.
m2.coat2: In the pocket, a box of matches. From the tavern.
m2.coatEmpty: Dad's coat. The pockets are empty.
m2.body1: There's a shape under the sheet. Long. Still.
m2.body2: It breathed. I swear it breathed.
m2.body3: I'm not lifting that sheet. Not now.
m2.scratch1: On the inside of the door, low down, at a child's height: LISA, LISA, LISA. Scratched with fingernails.
m2.scratch2: I wrote that. While she, outside, was screaming my name.
m2.cellaMeat: Frozen carcasses, one after another. The hook creaks.
m2.cantina1: The cellar. The floor is marked, as if something had been drawn on it and then rubbed out.
m2.cantina2: At the back, a small table and a chair. Someone sat down here to wait for Dad.
uv.m2ritual1: Salt in a circle. Five flames: one for every memory given back.
uv.m2ritual2: In the middle, something of mine.
uv.m2ritual3: Then call him, Diego. The way you called him when you were little. — L.
m2.ritualReadSay: Lisa knew how to free him. Salt in a circle, five candles lit, something of hers in the middle. Then I have to call him.
note.m2.ritual: Cellar (Lisa's ink): 1) salt in a circle on the floor; 2) light the five candles; 3) something of Lisa's in the middle; 4) call Dad, the way I did as a child.
m2.dontKnow: I don't know what to do with that here. The floor is marked, but I don't understand how.
m2.circle: The floor is marked: a circle, half rubbed out. Five candle stubs around it. Something must be written somewhere.
m2.circleNeed: The salt, the five candles lit, something of Lisa's in the middle. I'm still missing something.
m2.saltDone: I pour the salt along the mark. The circle closes.
m2.candlesDone: I light the five candles, one by one. The barber, Ada, the clockmaker, the photographer, the radio.
m2.ribbonTooSoon: First the salt circle and the candles, Lisa wrote.
m2.ribbonDone: I lay Lisa's ribbon in the middle of the circle. Every flame bends towards it.
m2.bruno3: I HAVE NO CHILDREN. I ONLY HAVE DEBTS.
m2.shoutText: Call him. Loud, the way you called him as a child: «DAD!»
m2.notYet: My voice won't come. He's still there, in the circle. I have to call him.
m2.free2: It's me, Dad. Lisa hid me in the cold room. I remember everything now.
m2.free3: It wasn't me holding the cleaver. It was his thing. The one he sold me, the man in black.
m2.free4: That day he took Lisa. He shut her in the suitcase. And on the counter he left this.
m2.free5: Go to her, Diego. Bring her home. And forgive me, if you can.
m2.after1: He's gone. The candles went out all at once.
m2.after2: Lisa's ribbon is still there. I take it back: I'll bring it to her myself.
m2.circleDone: The salt circle, the candles out. There's nobody here any more.
m2.chair: A chair, turned towards the circle. He sat on this chair.
m2.jars: Jars of preserves. In the last one, at the back, something floats. It isn't a peach.

I, Bruno, receive as a gift what I desire:
that the grief for my wife may touch me no more.
In return, one delivery every Tuesday.

Signed: Bruno

m2.contractSay: Dad's deal with the man in black. «That the grief for my wife may touch me no more.» Mum.

A black card, smooth as glass. Silver letters:

Well Alley, at the far end

mem.bruno.title: Memory — Bruno
mem.bruno.1: 1955. Dad marries Mum, at St Michael's. He with his moustache freshly trimmed, she in the veil Ada sewed for her.
mem.bruno.2: 1958. The Premiata Macelleria: Dad behind the counter, with his shop boys. The prize hangs in the window.
mem.bruno.3: Sundays in the country, Lisa and me with Mum and Dad. He pulls faces to make us laugh.
mem.bruno.4: Mum. The last winter, before she fell ill.
mem.bruno.5: 1973. Mum is gone. Dad spends his nights in the curing room, alone, among the hams. He doesn't talk any more.
diary.memBruno.title: Memory: Bruno, my father
diary.memBruno.text:
1955: Dad marries Mum.
1958: the Premiata Macelleria.
Sundays in the country, with Lisa and me.
1973: Mum dies, and Dad goes out like a light.
October 1974: the Emporium window, the man in black, the deal, the deliveries «downstairs».
On the 24th of October it wasn't him holding the cleaver.
I called him, and he went in peace. He left me the Suitcase Maker's card.

item.cellarkey.desc: A black key, greasy. It opens the padlock on the trapdoor in the curing room.
item.salt.desc: Coarse salt, for the hams. Lisa wrote: salt in a circle.
item.matches.desc: A box of tavern matches, from Dad's pocket. Enough for a few candles.
item.ribbon.desc: The white ribbon Lisa had in her hair on the 24th of October.
item.blackcard.desc: The card the man in black left on Dad's counter. Tap it twice to read it.
hint.m2.ledger: Dad's ledger, on the counter. Read it to the end: my handwriting is there.
hint.m2.scale: The scale: the drawer opens at the weight of the last delivery in the ledger.
hint.m2.labDoor: You have the curing room key: use it on the door on the left, under the stairs.
hint.m2.labUv: In the workroom I left some writing, above the bench.
hint.m2.grinder: The grinder: get close and turn the crank with your finger, anticlockwise, three times.
hint.m2.trapdoor: The trapdoor in the curing room floor: open the padlock with the cellar key.
hint.m2.ritualUv: In the cellar, on the back wall, it says how to free him.
hint.m2.salt: Salt: there's a full bin in the curing room.
hint.m2.saltUse: Pour the salt on the circle marked on the cellar floor.
hint.m2.matches: To light the candles you need fire. Dad kept matches in his coat, in the cold room.
hint.m2.matchesUse: Use the matches on the circle to light the five candles.
hint.m2.ribbon: Something of mine: my ribbon. I lost it in the cold room, it's in the ice. Breathe on it.
hint.m2.ribbonUse: Lay my ribbon in the middle of the circle.
hint.m2.call: Tap the circle and call him, loud. Dad.
hint.m2.leave: Dad is free. Now come to me: the Suitcase Maker's, at the end of the alley.
hint.map.butcher2: Dad is still in the butcher's. Before you come to me, free him.
hint.map.valigia: The black card: the Suitcase Maker's, at the end of the alley, right of the square. I'm waiting.
map.butcherDone: The Premiata Macelleria. The neon is off. For the first time, it's quiet inside.
map.alleyFather: The Suitcase Maker's alley, full of fog. Not yet: Dad is waiting for me at the butcher's.
map.alleyCard: The alley. The fog parts before the black card.
emp.afterCrypt1: You remember now, don't you? The boy in the cold room. What a pity.
emp.afterCrypt2: Your father is waiting for you. He never stopped waiting.
emp.afterBruno1: You've silenced the butcher. That wasn't the deal, boy.
emp.afterBruno3: Oh, you still owe me a suitcase. And inside it is something you care about.
end2.1:
Bruno rests.
In the square, the fog opens onto an alley.
end2.2:
At the end of the alley there's a window full of suitcases.
One, up high, is red.
m2.wall: The tiles above the bench. There's a smudge, as if someone had written with a wet finger. In normal light I can't read it.
m2.wallUv: Something is written on the wall here... Look closely.
m2.wallRead: Lisa's writing: the key in the grinder, turn it backwards.
m2.cantinaWall: The back wall. The plaster is marked with thin lines, nearly invisible. Written with something I can't see.
m2.ritualWall: Salt in a circle, five flames, something of Lisa's in the middle. Then call him.
retro.valveTap: Three red handwheels, numbered 0 to 9. How should I set them to get steam? Maybe the plate on the boiler says.
retro.valveTapPlate: Three red handwheels, numbered 0 to 9. The plate says 2 · 7 · 4. Turn them by running a finger round in a circle on top.
uv.wallSeen: Lisa's writing. I've already read it: it's in my notes.
uv.wallAim: Here, on the wall, something is written.
uv.wallLens: There's an odd stain on the wall, like dried ink. With the UV lens on the torch I might read it.
uv.wallNoLens: There's an odd stain on the wall, like dried ink. I can't read anything.
v.enter1: The suitcase maker's. Suitcases up to the ceiling, every one shut.
v.enter2: Some of them are breathing. I swear: they swell and sink, slowly.

Orders for the gentleman in black:

Grey leather suitcase — for A. M., barber. Delivered.
Small suitcase — for Mrs Ada. Delivered.
Travel case — for P. S., radio ham. Delivered.
Small suitcase, red — for Miss L.
Combination: the day she went away.
